Batch 4G skill 2/5. Scope Operator-derived. Boundary INVERTED from skills 1/shear: bending_moment_internal_loading and shear_force_internal_loading find V and M at ONE cut by section equilibrium and excluded the differential relations; THIS skill owns those relations and cites the siblings for point values. Worked example Operator-re-derived: 6 m simply-supported beam, uniform w=4 kN/m, Ay=By=12, V(0+)=12. dV/dx = -w = -4 kN/m (the minus is load-bearing: downward w gives decreasing shear; +4 would reverse the sense and misplace the extremum). ΔV = -area under w = -(4)(6) = -24 kN, checked V(6-)=12-24=-12. V(x)=12-4x, V=0 at x=3 m, where dM/dx=V=0 so M has a local extremum - and the example states the extremum is NOT at max|w| or max|V| (which are at the ends), the exact misconception the skill owns. signed_procedure_worked_example.prompt: A beam of total length 12 m has a pin at A (x = 0), a roller at B (x = 8 m), and a free overhang to C (x = 12 m). A downward uniform load w = 4 kN/m acts over the entire length. Reactions are Ay = 12 kN upward and By = 36 kN upward. The shear and moment diagrams have already been constructed (cite shear_moment_diagram_construction). From that diagram: V(0+) = +12 kN, V = 0 at x = 3 m and at the free end x = 12 m, V(8−) = −20 kN, V(8+) = +16 kN; M(0) = 0, M(3) = +18 kN·m, M(8) = −32 kN·m, M(12) = 0. Identify all candidate stations for extreme moment, compare their |M| values, and report the numeric global maximum bending moment with its location and sign. Do not reconstruct the full diagrams as the deliverable.
solution_steps: Diagram given (skill 3): V and M key values stated in the prompt. Relations cited: dM/dx = V so interior extrema occur at V = 0; global max = largest |M| among all candidates.
Candidate stations: V = 0 at x = 3 m; V = 0 at free end x = 12 m; support B at x = 8 m; pin end A at x = 0. (Free end C coincides with the V = 0 at x = 12 m.)
M at each candidate (from the given diagram / area-under-V results already on the diagram): M(0) = 0; M(3) = +18 kN·m (sagging); M(8) = −32 kN·m (hogging over the overhang support); M(12) = 0.
Compare magnitudes: |M(3)| = 18 kN·m; |M(8)| = 32 kN·m; ends 0. The first V = 0 station (x = 3 m) is NOT the global max. Largest |M| is 32 kN·m at x = 8 m.
Global maximum: M = −32 kN·m (hogging) at x = 8 m (support B). Report value, location, and sign — not a full re-drawn diagram.

signed_procedure_worked_example.prompt: A 6 m simply-supported beam is pinned at A (left end) and has a roller at B (right end). A downward uniform load w = 4 kN/m acts over the entire span. Support reactions are Ay = 12 kN upward and By = 12 kN upward. Using the load-shear-moment relations (cite shear_moment_load_relationships), construct the complete shear and moment diagrams across the beam: give V and M at every key point, state the segment degrees, verify closure, and mark the M value where V = 0. Do not re-solve section equilibrium at many cuts. Do not treat numeric global-max-M extraction as the deliverable.
solution_steps: Reactions given: Ay = 12 kN up at x = 0, By = 12 kN up at x = 6 m. Uniform w = 4 kN/m downward on 0 ≤ x ≤ 6 m.

Relations (cited): dV/dx = −w; ΔM = ∫ V dx; upward concentrated force → V jumps up; downward concentrated force → V jumps down. Convention: w positive downward; V positive upward on left face; M positive sagging.

V diagram (left to right). Just left of A: V = 0. At A, jump +Ay → V(0+) = +12 kN. Under the UDL, dV/dx = −4 kN/m so V decreases linearly: V(x) = 12 − 4x. Key points: V(3) = 0; V(6−) = 12 − 24 = −12 kN. At B, jump +By → V(6+) = −12 + 12 = 0. Closure OK. Segment 0–6: V is linear (degree 1).
Order gate: the V diagram is complete at all key points. Only now construct M from areas under V. (Attempting M before this step would leave ΔM = ∫ V dx without a determined V diagram.)

M diagram from V. M(0) = 0 (simple support). From x = 0 to x = 3: V is a triangle of base 3 m and height 12 kN → area = (1/2)(3)(12) = 18 kN·m → M(3) = 0 + 18 = 18 kN·m. From x = 3 to x = 6: V is a triangle below the axis, area = −(1/2)(3)(12) = −18 kN·m → M(6) = 18 − 18 = 0. Closure OK (simple support at B). Under the UDL, V is linear → M is parabolic (degree 2) on 0–6.
V = 0 at x = 3 m; the diagram peak is M(3) = 18 kN·m. Report the diagrams (key points + degrees), not a standalone global-max-M claim.
Complete diagrams: V: 0 −(+12)→ +12 (at 0+) → linear to 0 (at 3 m) → linear to −12 (at 6−) −(+12)→ 0 (at 6+). M: 0 (at 0) → parabolic to 18 kN·m (at 3 m) → parabolic to 0 (at 6 m).

signed_procedure_worked_example.prompt: A 6 m simply-supported beam is pinned at A (left end) and has a roller at B (right end). A downward uniform load w = 4 kN/m acts over the entire span. Support reactions are Ay = 12 kN upward and By = 12 kN upward. Just to the right of A, the internal shear is V(0+) = Ay = 12 kN (positive upward on the left face). Using dV/dx = −w and the area form of the shear relation, find (1) the shear slope under the distributed load, (2) the change in shear ΔV from just right of A to just left of B, and (3) the location between A and B where V = 0, stating the consequence for M. Do not construct the full shear or moment diagrams, and do not compute the numeric maximum moment.
solution_steps: Relations and convention: dV/dx = −w, dM/dx = V; ΔV = −∫ w dx. w positive downward; V positive upward on the left face.
Given: w = 4 kN/m downward on 0 ≤ x ≤ 6 m; V(0+) = Ay = 12 kN.
Under the uniform load, dV/dx = −w = −4 kN/m. The minus is required: downward w > 0 produces a decreasing shear along +x. (Writing dV/dx = +4 would reverse the sense of the shear change.)
Area under w from A+ to B−: ∫₀⁶ w dx = (4 kN/m)(6 m) = 24 kN. Therefore ΔV = −24 kN. Check: V(6−) = V(0+) + ΔV = 12 + (−24) = −12 kN.

Along the span, V(x) = 12 − 4x (kN, x in m). Set V = 0: 12 − 4x = 0 → x = 3 m. At x = 3 m, dM/dx = V = 0, so M has a local extremum there. The extremum is not located by maximizing |w| or |V| (here |V| is largest at the ends).
Report: dV/dx = −4 kN/m; ΔV = −24 kN from A+ to B−; V = 0 at x = 3 m (M local extremum). Stop — no full diagrams, no numeric M_max.
